jurisdiction.name: Barbados
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Barbados has no AI strategy, AI law or AI guidance. Its only AI-relevant national instrument is the Data Protection Act, 2019-29, which gives people a right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing and requires data protection impact assessments for automated profiling. A Centre for AI Innovation and Governance has been announced but no founding document is published.
lead_institutions: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
Ministry of Industry, Innovation, Science and Technology
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026. The data protection commissioner's and the innovation ministry's websites could not be accessed, and online Official Gazette issues after 2020 could not be searched, so only one document could be read. Barbados is marked for a later retry. The planned AI centre and the cybercrime bill are tracked as leads.

instruments.current_status: Enacted (Governor-General's assent 12 August 2019) and published as a Supplement to Official Gazette No. 66 of 15 August 2019. Section 100 provides that the Act comes into operation on a date fixed by proclamation; the commencement proclamation (reported by secondary sources as bringing most of the Act into force on 31 March 2021, with the controller/processor registration provisions excepted) was not read on an official source, so effective_date is left null. The bill (as amended by a Joint Select Committee) is on barbadosparliament.com (bills/details/417).
instruments.summary: Barbados's GDPR-modelled data protection law regulating the collection, keeping, processing, use and dissemination of personal data by data controllers and processors, supervised by a Data Protection Commissioner. Section 18 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects (with contract, enactment and consent exceptions and required safeguards, and a stricter rule for sensitive data), and data subjects must be informed of the existence of automated decision-making and its logic. A data protection impact assessment is required for systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects based on automated processing, including profiling, on which significant decisions are based.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only national legislation with explicit rules on automated decision-making and profiling; governs AI systems that process personal data.

leads.title: Cybercrime Bill, 2024
leads.note: Bill (Objects and Reasons dated 2024-01-29) to repeal the Computer Misuse Act, Cap. 124B; referred to a Joint Select Committee in the Senate (barbadosparliament.com). The tabled text (https://www.barbadosparliament.com/uploads/bill_resolution/48c581fc50f5357214a37caab9189066.pdf) contains no explicit AI or deepfake provision; commentary says it would cover AI-generated child abuse material. Re-check only if an enacted version adds AI/synthetic-media provisions.
